coding.notes: Appeal Nos. 2014-1360 and 2014-1500 consolidated from E.D. Tex. (Schneider, J.). issues.quote: We perceive no legal error or abuse of discretion in the Board's determination that Dr. Christian did not show good cause for her delay.

coding.author: PER CURIAM
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition. Affirmance of MSPB dismissal as untimely. issues.description: Standing: whether CGI was an interested party (actual or prospective bidder with a direct economic interest) despite not submitting a bid.
issues.quote: Because CGI was a prospective bidder with a direct economic interest affected by the award of the contract, we conclude that CGI had standing to file its protest in the Court of Federal Claims.

issues.description: Bid protest merits: the 2014 RFQ payment terms violate FAR Part 12's prohibition on terms inconsistent with customary commercial practice, so the protest is sustained.
issues.quote: the revised payment terms violate FAR Part 12's prohibition against including contract terms inconsistent with customary commercial practice, we reverse the Court of Federal Claims grant of judgment on the administrative record to the government.

issues.description: Forfeiture and waiver: the government's argument that the Court of Federal Claims lacked authority to find the payment terms inconsistent with customary commercial practice was deemed waived.
issues.quote: We deem this issue waived by the government.

coding.author: Moore
coding.notes: Pre-award bid protest. The court held CGI remained a prospective bidder after filing a timely GAO protest and that the three-business-day gap before filing in the CFC did not defeat standing. The court did not reach CGI's alternative FASA and unduly-restrictive-competition grounds. The jurisdictional statement under 28 U.S.C. § 1295(a)(3) is routine and not coded. Unanimous panel with no dissent.

issues.description: Construction of claim 7 of the '343 patent (mounting plate 'substantially planar' and 'oriented perpendicular to the drive wheel axis'), which the court reversed, removing the basis for cancellation of claim 7.
issues.quote: It is unreasonable to read that straightforward language as meaning anything other than that the drive-wheel axis is perpendicular to the surface of the mounting plate that makes the plate substantially planar.

issues.description: Obviousness of the remaining claims of the '598 and '343 patents over Goertzen combined with Hosino (and Schaffner or Mulhern), including motivation to lower the pivot and the reasonable expectation of compensating for instability; the court affirmed cancellation.

coding.author: Taranto
coding.notes: Appeal from IPR2013-00407 and IPR2013-00411 (consolidated Nos. 2015-1585, 2015-1586). Decided April 5, 2016. Reversed in part and affirmed in part. No separate opinions or dissents appear in the text provided.

issues.description: Jurisdiction: Federal Circuit's limited jurisdiction under 38 U.S.C. 7292 to review Veterans Court decisions; appeal challenging factual findings and application of law to fact dismissed for lack of jurisdiction
issues.quote: Because the only issue here is Mr. Swearingen's disagreement with factual findings and application of law to fact, we must dismiss the appeal for lack of jurisdiction.

coding.author: PER CURIAM
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition. The court dismissed the appeal under 38 U.S.C. 7292 and did not reach the merits of service connection or duty-to-assist issues, so no merits codes were assigned.

issues.quote: In order to maintain a claim for breach of contract, a party must be in privity with the United States.

coding.author: O'Malley
coding.notes: Affirmed the Court of Federal Claims in full. Takings ripeness is coded X01 because the court did not reach the takings merits. Case mixes a government-lease breach claim with a takings claim; case type chosen as Government contracts because the dominant claim is a contract claim against the government.

issues.quote: Because we conclude that the district court did not abuse its discretion in finding that SFA's litigating position and the manner in which it litigated this case did not stand out, we affirm the district court's determination that Newegg failed to establish that this case is exceptional under § 285.

coding.author: O'Malley
coding.notes: Single issue: § 285 fee denial affirmed under Octane Fitness abuse-of-discretion review. coding.author: PER CURIAM
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition affirming MSPB decision denying FERS disability retirement application as untimely. Discovery argument was raised only in a footnote without explanation and not separately coded. No dissents.

coding.notes: Appeal from E.D. Tex. (Schneider, J.) summary judgment of noninfringement after claim construction. issues.description: ITC threat of material injury finding by Commissioner Pinkert, which was counted toward the affirmative vote; the court held substantial evidence supported the threat finding.

issues.description: Prospective-only effective date of countervailing duties under the Special Rule (19 U.S.C. §§ 1671e(b), 1673e(b)); the court held the earlier Federal Circuit ruling in Wind Tower Trade Coalition is the law of the case and declined to reconsider it.

coding.case_type: Trademark
coding.side_a_parties: Simon Shiao Tam (applicant, THE SLANTS mark)
coding.side_b_parties: Michelle K. Lee, Director, United States Patent and Trademark Office

issues.description: Section 2(a) disparagement bar (15 U.S.C. 1052(a)): the court held the disparagement provision unconstitutional, so the bar on registering Tam's mark falls and the Board's unregistrability holding is vacated.
issues.quote: We hold that the disparagement provision of § 2(a) is unconstitutional because it violates the First Amendment. We vacate the Board's holding that Mr. Tam's mark is unregistrable, and remand this case to the Board for further proceedings.

issues.description: Constitutional challenge: First Amendment challenge to the § 2(a) disparagement provision, held to succeed on its face under strict scrutiny (with alternative holding under Central Hudson).
issues.quote: The government cannot refuse to register disparaging marks because it disapproves of the expressive messages conveyed by the marks. The government regulation at issue amounts to viewpoint discrimination, and under the strict scrutiny review appropriate for government regulation of message or viewpoint, we conclude that the disparagement proscription of § 2(a) is unconstitutional.

coding.author: Moore
coding.notes: En banc decision (corrected) on the constitutionality of the Lanham Act section 2(a) disparagement bar. Majority opinion by Moore joined by Prost, Newman, O'Malley, Wallach, Taranto, Chen, Hughes and Stoll. O'Malley concurred separately (joined by Wallach) on vagueness grounds under the Fifth Amendment. Dyk concurred in part and dissented in part (joined by Lourie and Reyna as to parts I-IV), agreeing the bar is unconstitutional as applied to Tam but not facially or as to commercial speech. Lourie and Reyna each dissented. Footnote 3 reinstates the panel's holding that the mark is disparaging, but the registrability holding is vacated on constitutional grounds. Only the constitutional and registrability issues are coded; no other section 2 provisions were decided.
